10041609:
Amy Hughes Kittery LD 330
My name is Amy Hughes, and I am a resident of Kittery, Maine. I am writing to express my support for LD 330. Maine's criminal code, like those of many states, has evolved over decades--often through piecemeal amendments in response to specific incidents, political pressures, or social changes. As a result, it contains outdated, redundant, and sometimes contradictory provisions that can undermine the clarity, consistency, and fairness of our justice system.
This bill takes a thoughtful, inclusive, and expert-driven approach by bringing together diverse legal perspectives and ensuring a transparent and professional review process led by an experienced outside consultant. This also allows for input from state departments and agencies with practical knowledge of how these laws are implemented.
A coherent criminal code is essential for protecting individual rights; reducing wrongful prosecutions or legal confusion; promoting efficient court procedures, and ensuring consistent and equitable application of justice across the state. This is not about overhauling the substance of our laws overnight--it's about clarity, accuracy, and modernization. And by requiring a full report by February 1, 2026, this process is both time-bound and accountable.
I urge this committee to support LD 330 and help lay the groundwork for a fairer and more effective criminal justice system in Maine.
Thank you for your time and your commitment to public service.
Respectfully submitted,
Amy Hughes Kittery, Maine

While the Judicial Branch takes no position on LD 330, we would like to make one point regarding the membership of the advisory council created by the resolve. The advisory council includes an active retired judge or justice, rather than a full-time appointed judge or justice. Because active retired judges are paid on a per-diem basis, we will have to estimate the amount of a judge's time that would be spent as part of the council and add a fiscal note to the proposal. TO: Senator Anne Beebe-Center Representative Tavis Hasenfus Joint Standing Committee on Criminal Justice and Public Safety

RE: LD 330, Resolve, to Create an Advisory Council to Oversee the Review and Technical Revision of the Maine Criminal Code and Other Statutes Establishing Criminal Offenses
DA: March 31, 2025
The Criminal Law Advisory Commission (CLAC)* respectfully submits the following testimony neither for nor against LD 330.
CLAC supports the aim of the bill and its focus on technical revision of the Criminal Code and other statutes establishing criminal offenses. We support the concept of a small, non-partisan group to undertake the type of objective review proposed. The tasks identified in the bill of identifying obsolete provisions, clarifying language, eliminating inconsistences and consolidating or eliminating redundant provisions are consistent with CLAC's goals as we review proposed legislation and are often reflected in the recommendations CLAC offers to the Legislature. For additional context, LD 1903 (131st Leg.) and CLAC's testimony in response (May 23, 2023).
Given the extent of the work anticipated, the projected completion date is unrealistic. The effort would have to be appropriately funded to attract a consultant with the requisite knowledge and experience as well as support staff.
*CLAC is an advisory body established by the Legislature. 17-A M.R.S. �� 1351-1357. It consists of 9 members appointed by the Attorney General. Our current members include defense attorneys, prosecutors, Maine Bar Counsel, and a retired practitioner with experience as defense counsel, prosecutor and in court administration. In addition, three sitting judges and one retired practitioner, appointed by the Chief Justice of the Supreme Judicial Court, and, by statute, the CoChairs of the Legislature's Committee on Criminal Justice and Public Safety, serve as consultants. The Supreme Judicial Court's Criminal Process Manager serves as liaison from the Court to CLAC. CLAC advises the Legislature on matters relating to crimes in the Criminal Code and in other Titles, the Bail and Juvenile Codes, and with respect to other statutes related to criminal justice processes.

Dear Senator Beebe-Center, Representative Hasenfus, and Members of the Committee on Criminal Justice and Public Safety:
MACDL supports LD 330. Maine's Criminal Code underwent its last comprehensive revision in 1976. As this Committee is aware, the Criminal Code changes every session in response to present day priorities of criminal justice in Maine. As a result, the Criminal Code is made up of countless revisions and additions. These revision and addition are not always written in harmony with prior parts of the code. These revisions and additions likewise can become unnecessary vestiges.
LD 330 establishes an Advisory Council to oversee a technical review and revision of Maine's Criminal Code. This review and revision is necessary given the passage of time since any prior significant review.

Notwithstanding its support, MACDL does recommend that the Advisory Council be better balanced by including an additional defense attorney or removing one prosecutor. LD 330 proposes that the Advisory Counsel be made up of a prosecutor, a defense attorney, a legal educator with expertise in criminal law, an active retired judge, and a designee of the Attorney General. The Attorney General will undoubtedly send an employee with criminal experience such as a current or former criminal prosecutor. As a result, the Advisory Council will be imbalanced with unnecessary emphasis on prosecution. MACDL recommends an additional member of the defense bar be appointed or one of the two prosecutor positions be removed. MACDL further seeks its input in addition to the Maine Commission on Public Defense Services. MACDL has testified before this Committee and sent participants to legislative

Good aftemoon, Senator Beebe-Center, Representative Hasenfus, and friends and colleagues on
the best committee in the Maine Legislature. My name is Nina Milliken and I am lucky to
represent the communities of Blue Hill, Brooksville, Castine, Sedgwick, Sun'y and Trenton in
the Maine House. I am happy to be here today to present my bill, LD 330, Resolve, To Create
an Advisory Council to Oversee the Review and Technical Revision of the Maine Criminal
Code and Other Statutes Establishing Criminal Offenses.

Last sunnner, I reached out to Julie Fimi from the Judicial Branch and asked if it was possible to get a list of all active criminal codes in the state. I got a nearly 80-page list. I have brought a
couple copies of the list with me today. In addition to all of the current criminal statutes, you will
notice that the list provides some other information, specifically, the class of each offense, when the law came into effect, the last time a case was filed, how many cases have been filed and the number of days since the offense was last used. As you flip through the pages, you will notice that a significant percentage of the criminal statutes have never been charged and many have been charged less than l0 times. Some have been in the books for decades and some came into
effect in the last couple of years.

Some of the crimes that have never been charged should be crimes. For example, "Causing a catastrophe," thank goodness, has never been charged but it should be illegal to commit this offense. But I assert that many of the offenses listed are perhaps dated or frivolous. If a law has been on the books for several years in Maine like the Class C offense of transporting Christmas
trees without permission, which has been on the books since 2004 and never charged, is there
much need for it?

This resolve would pull together a group of stakeholders to go through all of Title 17 and other sections of the law that establish criminal statutes to identify unused and obsolete provisions,

10040830:
Testimony in support of LD 330 the Committee on Criminal Justice and Public Safety
March 31, 2025
Senator Beebe-Center, Representative Hasenfus and distinguished members of the Committee:
My name is Sarah Johnson and I am a resident of Sanford. I am writing in support of LD 330, Resolve, to Create an Advisory Council to Oversee the Review and Technical Revision of the Maine Criminal Code and Other Statutes Establishing Criminal Offenses.
I support this bill for many reasons. The most glaring is the overwhelming volume of bills presented in this and previous legislative sessions that are focused on punitive measures, increasing incarceration time for crimes already defined and increasing the number of defined crimes. The negative impact to our families, communities and individuals of increased incarceration is physical, emotional and economic. We do not seem capable of investing thought into more diversion programs, support systems, community service alternatives or restorative processes. I am confident that this diverse, professional and unbiased Advisory Council will consider public safety and community well being in their work. I hope you will support LD 330 and create this much needed council and process.
Thank you for your time and consideration. Sarah Johnson Sanford, Maine.
